sources.summary: Encyclopedia overview of LGBT rights in Brazil: relationship recognition (same-sex unions 2011, marriage 2013), the Supreme Federal Tribunal's 2018 self-declaration gender-identity rulings and treatment of non-binary markers, conversion-therapy and blood-donation positions, sections on anti-LGBT violence, religion and politics, and a summary table of legal status; used in the country dossier for the national legal baseline against which state-level counts and ordinances diverge.

International LGBT-rights organisation's Brazil country overview (updated 12 March 2026): same-sex relations legal and legal gender recognition possible by self-determination, LGBTI organisations able to register; marriage equality since 2013 with active congressional repeal efforts driven by anti-gender lawmakers; a 2019 Supreme Court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds, yet Brazil keeps one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; over 3,000 openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections.

Brazilian law-firm guide (updated 5 April 2026) to LGBTQ+ legal rights for expats: Brazil has no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute, but Supreme Federal Tribunal rulings establish progressive protections - same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, adoption, and name/gender-marker changes; cited in the dossier as the practical statement of the protective federal framework that state and municipal enforcement operates within.
